title: torpdata CI pipeline
about: What torpdata's GitHub Actions do on a match day, in order, and how long each part takes. Two workflows: the Daily Data Release (fetches the new match data from the AFL and uploads it to the torpdata releases, then tells torp to recompute ratings) and, later in the same chain, Build blog data (starts after torp finishes its ratings and predictions, and puts the data the site reads on the R2 store). The ratings and predictions themselves are computed by the torp repository's workflow, described in that repo's guide.

pipelines.name: Daily data release
pipelines.about: One job. It fetches the latest match data from the AFL API and uploads it to the torpdata GitHub releases (chains, play-by-play, player stats, fixtures, results, teams, player details, player game data, derived ratings, injuries). Most runs find nothing new and stop after about two minutes, mainly spent installing R, so they say nothing about a real release and are left out. The guide cannot tell a no-new-data run from a real one except by how it was started, so it counts only manual (Run workflow) runs that took over 5.5 minutes. Among the last 100 successful runs (25 Oct to 25 Nov 2026, the off-season) exactly one released data: the manual run of 26 Oct. So the timings below are ONE run, not a median of five. In the season, scheduled runs that release data will not be counted until the select rule is changed to include them; no-new-data runs that happen to be slow (installing R took up to 17 minutes in some) would then have to be filtered out some other way.
pipelines.triggers: Started by GitHub's schedule: a run every few hours after games on Thursday to Monday (the times in the workflow file are written as Sydney winter time, AEST, so an hour later in summer) and a daily safety net at 2am AEST; or by hand with Run workflow (force_release skips the new-games check, rebuild_aggregates rebuilds every season since 2021). When it releases data it dispatches the ratings-trigger event to the torp repository, which starts torp's Daily Ratings & Predictions run; that run's timings are in torp's own guide, and its end starts the Build blog data pipeline below.

steps.name: Run daily release
steps.about: Runs run_daily_release() from torp's data-raw/01-data/daily_release.R. It first decides between a full release (a match ended in the last 12 hours, or one finished in the last 48 hours is missing from a released file, or the run was forced), a team-only release (no new games but the team lineups changed) and nothing. A full release updates the chains and play-by-play files, then expected goals, fixtures, results, player stats, teams, player details, player game data and score events, then the derived player game ratings, player season ratings, expected-points and win-probability chart data, PSR (player stat ratings) and weather, and always an injury snapshot. Each file goes to its own torpdata release

steps.name: Verify release uploads
steps.about: Checks that the key files (play-by-play, chains and player stats, or the teams file for a team-only release) were uploaded in the last 24 hours; if none were, torp is not told to run

steps.name: Wait for release-list propagation

pipelines.name: Build blog data
pipelines.about: One job. It takes the ratings and predictions that torp has just released, joins them with the match, player and shot data into the parquet files the inthegame-blog site reads (ratings, predictions, game logs, shots, season simulations, team strength and so on), and uploads them to the Cloudflare R2 store under inthegame-data/afl/. All five most recent runs are counted.
pipelines.triggers: Started by the torp repository's Daily Ratings & Predictions run, whose last step sends the blog-trigger event here; or by hand. It shares its queue (concurrency group daily-release) with the Daily Data Release above, so it waits if a release is running. It starts nothing else: the site reads the files it uploads.

jobs.name: build
jobs.about: Builds the blog's parquet files from the torpdata releases and uploads them to R2

steps.name: Set up job
steps.about: GitHub starts the machine and downloads the actions this job uses

steps.name: Run actions/checkout@v7
steps.about: Downloads this repo's code onto the machine

steps.name: Checkout torp package (for simulations)
steps.about: Downloads the torp package, which the season simulations and the team-name tidying need

steps.name: Run r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
steps.about: Installs R

steps.name: Run r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
steps.about: Installs the R packages this repo needs (from a cache when it can)

steps.name: Download source parquets
steps.about: Downloads the inputs from the torpdata releases: team and player ratings, predictions (including the backfilled and retrodiction ones), player details, play-by-play, per-game ratings, raw game stats, fixtures and the shot model; stops the run if a required set is incomplete

steps.name: Aggregate
steps.about: Runs scripts/build_blog_data.R: builds the blog's ratings, team ratings, predictions, player details, game logs and game stats, shots, injuries and the Monte Carlo season simulations and team strength files, into blog/

steps.name: Build AFL chain parquet (per-row WP/WPA-credit chain data)
steps.about: Runs scripts/build_afl_chains.R: builds the season's chain-events file (every event in the chain feed with expected points and running score) and the player-quarters file (each player's expected points added and win probability added per quarter)

steps.name: Rebuild + publish player skills history
steps.about: Joins the per-season player stat ratings into one all-seasons history and republishes it to the player_skills-data release (no recomputing; a failure only warns)

steps.name: Download extra parquets for R2
steps.about: Downloads files torp has already released and renames them for the site: team lineups, the finals matchup table, player skills (and the latest row per player), the net points breakdown and the skills history; each is optional and a missing one only warns

steps.name: Validate outputs
steps.about: Stops the run if any of the required files is missing (ratings, team ratings, predictions, player details, game logs); only warns about missing optional ones such as simulations and shots

steps.name: Snapshot dated predictions + injuries (torpdata#77)
steps.about: Saves a dated copy of today's predictions and injuries, so what the model said on a past day can be shown later

steps.name: Strip oversized R metadata from parquets
steps.about: Rewrites any file whose footer is over 1 MB so browsers do not download the extra R information (a failure here does not stop the run)

steps.name: Run actions/setup-node@v7
steps.about: Installs Node 20

steps.name: Install wrangler
steps.about: Installs Cloudflare's wrangler tool used for the upload

steps.name: Upload to R2
steps.about: Uploads every file in blog/ to the R2 store at inthegame-data/afl/, with up to 3 attempts per file

steps.about: Clean-up for an earlier step (saves caches, removes credentials)
